record.paper_title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
record.original_question: Does there exist a complete lattice L with enough co-primes, equivalently a complete lattice isomorphic as a lattice to the lattice of all closed subsets of some topological space, such that the Scott space Sigma L=(L, sigma(L)) is non-sober?

evidence.quote: Question 3.5. Is there a complete lattice with enough co-primes (i.e., isomorphic to the lattice of all closed subsets of a topological space) that has a non-sober Scott topology?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall the following definitions. A complete lattice is a partially ordered set in which every subset has a supremum (and hence an infimum). An element p of a complete lattice L is called co-prime if p ≠ ⊤ and whenever p ≥ x ∧ y for some x, y ∈ L, then p ≥ x or p ≥ y. The lattice L is said to have enough co-primes if every element of L is the infimum of the set of co-prime elements above it; equivalently, L is isomorphic, as a lattice, to the lattice of all closed subsets of some topological space (ordered by inclusion).

For a complete lattice L, a subset D ⊆ L is directed if every finite subset of D has an upper bound in D. A subset U ⊆ L is Scott-open if (i) U is an upper set (x ∈ U and x ≤ y imply y ∈ U) and (ii) for every directed set D ⊆ L with ⋁D ∈ U, we have D ∩ U ≠ ∅. The family σ(L) of all Scott-open subsets of L is a topology on L; the resulting topological space ΣL = (L, σ(L)) is called the Scott space of L.

A topological space X is sober if every nonempty irreducible closed subset of X (i.e., a nonempty closed set that is not the union of two proper closed subsets) is the closure of a unique point of X.

Question: Does there exist a complete lattice L with enough co-primes such that the Scott space ΣL is not sober?
artifact.status_search_result: The paper "On two problems about sobriety of topological spaces" (Topology and its Applications, 2021) explicitly addresses this question and constructs a closed set lattice (equivalently, a complete lattice with enough co-primes) whose Scott space is non-sober, providing an affirmative answer.

status_evidence.title: On two problems about sobriety of topological spaces - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: The paper answers two problems concerning sobriety: one concerns the existence of a closed set lattice whose Scott space is non-sober, and another is about the reflectivity of a category of k-bounded sober spaces.
status_evidence.claim: A closed set lattice with non-sober Scott topology is constructed, resolving the question affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: Some Recent Advances in Non-Hausdorff Topology
status_evidence.snippet: Xu, Xi and Zhao showed that there is a complete Heyting algebra whose Scott topology is not sober.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work confirms construction of complete lattices (even frames) whose Scott topology is non-sober.
